rounds.text: Alufluoride Ltd demonstrates exceptional fundamental strength, evidenced by a 5-year compounded profit growth of 116% [E17] and a trailing twelve-month profit surge of 71% [E19]. This robust profitability is underpinned by high capital efficiency, with return on equity reaching 22.0% [E13] and return on capital employed hitting 24.2% [E12], significantly outperforming sector benchmarks [E9, E10]. Operational execution is further highlighted by a cash conversion ratio of 1.88x for March 2026, confirming that reported profits are fully backed by strong cash generation [E31], alongside an operating margin expansion to 36% in September 2026 [E28]. Valuation metrics reveal a stark disconnect from these fundamental achievements, as a discounted cash flow model establishes an intrinsic value of Rs 1667 per share compared to the current market price of Rs 680 [E42], leaving a substantial margin of safety of 59.2% [E43]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF implies that today's price accounts for a mere 5.7% earnings growth against a base-case assumption of 18.0% [E44], while rules-based screening awards the company a high-confidence BUY score of 94 out of 100 [E57]. Conceded: compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months reads 0% [E16] and borrowings have increased to Rs 54 Cr in September 2026 from Rs 45 Cr a year prior [E36].

Despite recent earnings acceleration, a closer look at the fundamental record reveals structural vulnerabilities and stretched valuation metrics that the bull narrative glosses over. Sales growth has ground to a complete halt over the trailing twelve months, registering flat at 0% [E16] and directly contradicting longer-term top-line expansion. Conceded: the company boasts a high TTM profit growth of 71% [E19] and strong ROCE of 23.31% [E10]. However, this profitability rests on an "Inconsistent" yearly operating-margin trend over the last three years [E29] and an "Inconsistent" quarterly margin trend over the last two quarters [E30], signaling earnings volatility rather than stable compounding. Furthermore, leverage is climbing as borrowings increased to Rs 54 Cr in Sep 2026 from Rs 45 Cr a year prior [E36], coinciding with a domestic institutional retreat where institutional holdings dropped by 0.81 percentage points since December 2023 [E40]. Finally, the stock trades at a Price-to-Book multiple of 3.74x to 3.78x, which heavily outpaces the sector benchmark P/B of 1.76x [E2, E7], while exhibiting extreme annualised volatility of 57.0% [E50] right near its 52-week highs [E45, E46].

However, this top-line pause sits alongside a massive 71% TTM profit growth acceleration [E19] and a phenomenal quarterly operating margin surge of 36% in September 2026, up 11 percentage points year-over-year [E28]. Conceded: borrowings rose to Rs 54 Cr [E36], but this modest debt supports a pristine current ratio of 3.52x [E35] and is dwarfed by Rs 47 Cr in operating cash flow with a robust 1.88x cash conversion [E31]. Conceded: domestic institutional holdings declined [E40], yet overall institutional money flow is flagged as POSITIVE MONEY FLOW with a net holding increase of 0.47 percentage points [E41]. While the price-to-book multiple exceeds the sector benchmark [E7], the company easily justifies its premium through elite returns, delivering an ROE of 22.76% and an ROCE of 23.31% that both crush the broader sector benchmarks of 9.45% and 11.11% [E9, E10].

However, that outperformance against sector benchmarks comes alongside a steep price-to-book multiple of 3.74x compared to the sector benchmark of just 1.76x [E7]. Conceded: operating cash flow reached Rs 47 Cr [E32], but borrowings simultaneously climbed to Rs 54 Cr in September 2026, up from Rs 45 Cr a year earlier [E36]. Conceded: overall institutional money flow shows a positive designation [E41], yet domestic institutions have actively retreated, cutting their holdings from 1.28% to 0.47% [E40]. While quarterly margins improved [E28], the yearly operating-margin trend explicitly reads inconsistent over the last three years [E29]. Furthermore, trailing twelve months sales growth has completely stalled at 0% [E16], and annualized volatility runs very high at 57.0% [E50].
